---
title: Tool Comparison
---

## Quick reference

On the JupyterHub, the clinic provides pre-configured launchers for **Claude Code** (via the clinic's LiteLLM Bedrock gateway) and **Antigravity** (via Google Cloud). Other tools remain available for reference if running in your own environment.


| | Claude Code | Antigravity (`agy`) | OpenCode | Copilot CLI |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Hub launcher** | `claude-agent-coders` | `agy-agent-coders` | — | — |
| **Direct start** | `claude` | `agy` | `opencode` | `copilot` |
| **Credentials** | Workshop code / LiteLLM key | Google Cloud project code | Gateway key | GitHub / Gateway |
| **Switch model** | `/model name` | Settings / CLI args | `/models` menu | Env var restart |
| **Clear context** | `/clear` | `/clear` | — | — |
| **Instructions file** | `CLAUDE.md` or `AGENTS.md` | `AGENTS.md` | Config | System prompt |
| **Best for** | Claude models, deep reasoning | Gemini models, Google ecosystem | Open models | Quick suggestions |

## Key differences

**Claude Code** connects to the clinic's LiteLLM gateway on Amazon Bedrock. It has built-in commands for managing context (`/clear`), checking status and spending (`/status`, `/usage`, `claude-agent-coders --budget`), and switching models (`/model`). It reads `CLAUDE.md` or `@AGENTS.md` in the project root.

**Antigravity (`agy`)** is Google's agentic coding CLI powered by Gemini models. On the hub, the `agy-agent-coders` launcher installs `agy`, pre-approves everyday tasks (Quarto, R, Python, git, file inspections) so they run without interruption, and sets a safety guard that blocks destructive commands (`git reset --hard`, force push, `rm -r` outside project, pushing to `main`, deleting a repository) and makes the agent ask before merging, deleting branches or closing issues. The Claude Code launcher has no such guard; Claude Code's own permission prompts are the protection there. It reads `AGENTS.md` in the project root.

**OpenCode** is open-source and has flexible model configuration, connecting to open models through gateways.

**GitHub Copilot CLI** is focused on command-line suggestions and interactive coding assistance through GitHub Copilot.

## Common commands across tools

Regardless of which tool you use, you'll do the same basic things:

- **Give a prompt** — type what you want the agent to do
- **Approve tool use** — agents ask permission before running unapproved commands or modifying sensitive files
- **Review output** — always check what the agent did before moving on
- **End the session or reset** — close the tool or clear context (`/clear`) when switching tasks
